PullRequest.Title: sessions: suspend model comparison in non-Git folders
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #346583.

## Changes

- Hide comparison setup for confirmed non-Git folders, even when draft configuration supplies a default branch. Observe repository state so local initialization can enable comparison.
- Suspend retained comparisons in unsupported folders so the model pill and send action return to ordinary single-model chat. Restore comparison choices when the draft becomes eligible again.
- Keep comparisons armed while draft creation or configuration is pending, avoiding an unintended single-model send.
- Preserve folderless quick chats and locally initialized repositories, including unborn repositories without commits or a remote.

## Validation

- `corepack pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sessionComparisonModelSelection.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/compareAgentsSpotlight.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 249 tests.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts --grep 'observable availability distinguishes unknown, a non-repository, and git init|creates a populated clean worktree from an unborn repository snapshot' --reporter dot` — passed, 3 tests exercising actual Git initialization and unborn worktree creation.
- `corepack pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `corepack pnpm run eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/chat/newChatWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/chat/sessionComparisonModelSelection.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sessionComparisonModelSelection.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/compareAgentsSpotlight.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionComparisonModelPicker.fixture.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Live provider-backed Agents-window interaction, visual fixture rendering, and full integration/smoke suites were not run. This worktree has fresh client output but does not have compiled built-in extensions for a full dev-window launch.

## Manual Test

1. Enable `sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled` and configure two comparison models in a Git-backed new session.
2. Switch to a plain non-Git folder. Verify comparison setup is hidden, the Run Attempts label and comparison summary are absent, and a prompt can be sent normally.
3. Switch back to a Git repository or a folderless Chat. Verify the retained comparison choices return.
4. Run `git init` in a plain local folder, without adding a remote or making a commit. Verify comparison becomes available once repository/configuration state resolves and the existing unborn-repository comparison flow still works.
5. Switch between eligible workspaces while configuration loads. Verify retained comparisons do not send a single-model request during loading.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch the new-chat composer between Git-backed and confirmed non-Git folders, including running git init locally
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The availability derived observable recomputes comparison action state and the composer pill/send affordance. The added isRepository observable read is synchronous in-memory state access; no filesystem or subprocess work is awaited on this UI critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a local repository by looking for .git/config, with at most 50 parent-directory stat checks and bounded config reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolution is started per cached workspace key; repository state is capped at 50 workspace entries. The changed code only observes isRepository and does not call resolveRepository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repository resolution and getSessionTypesForFolder already existed. The comparison visibility calculation did not observe the resulting isRepository state and could continue past a confirmed false value when configuration supplied a branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution may populate the observable asynchronously when another existing provider path requests it; the added read itself does not start or await I/O. For confirmed non-Git folders, the new early return can avoid the later existing session-type lookup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected folder and one session repository are examined per recomputation; workspace folder matching is over the session folder list as before. Repository-state updates cause one derived recomputation, not per-file work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reactive recomputations are synchronous and dependency-tracked; repository resolution is coalesced per workspace key by _localGitRepositoryResolutionStarted. No new parallel boundary calls are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold local repository metadata may be unresolved until an existing caller invokes resolveRepository; warm state is reused from a per-provider cache capped at 50 entries. The diff neither changes cache keys nor adds miss retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line and repository implementations show an in-memory observable read with no resolver invocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository-state update frequency varies by provider, but the added operation is a single observable read and does not trigger boundary work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds bounded reactive work and can skip existing downstream provider/session-type work for confirmed non-repositories.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send from a draft that retains comparison choices after moving to an unsupported non-Git folder
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After workspace validation, enabled now becomes false once availability is conclusively false, so _send follows the ordinary single-model send path. This newly allows the user-requested send to make progress rather than failing the unavailable-comparison guard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare a session, create one chat through the selected provider, and send one request; provider implementations may cross process or network boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one ordinary session/chat request for one user send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A retained committed comparison stayed enabled even when unavailable, so _send entered _sendComparison and failed its availability check before launching any attempt or ordinary request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider create/send sequence is on the foreground send critical path, as required to fulfill the now-enabled single-model request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per explicit send; retained comparison choices are bounded by the existing maximum of 10 attempts but are not launched in this unsupported-folder scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One foreground send is awaited. Background mode retains its existing fire-and-forget behavior; the diff does not add a burst or change its limiter semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is used. Retained choices already lived in _committed before the change, so the diff does not increase retention lifetime or size.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: enabled gates _send directly, and the test added by the PR confirms one single-model request is sent while choices remain retained.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual provider latency varies, but it is required work for the explicit send rather than redundant work or a regression against a successful prior path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The additional provider operation is the intended successful replacement for a previously blocked user action, with constant cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep a configured comparison armed while draft/session creation or configuration resolution is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new pending observable keeps enabled true while session loading or configuration resolution is in progress. canSendRequest remains false because availability is false, so no send or comparison launch crosses an expensive boundary until pending state resolves.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session and one configuration-resolution observable; constant work per state transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No requests launch during pending state. Observable updates are coalesced through the existing derived graph and execute synchronously.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Committed selections remain in the existing in-memory observable. This was already retained before the diff and is bounded by the comparison attempt limit; no new cache or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: canSendRequest reads enabled, available, and configured and rejects the enabled-but-unavailable pending state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider configuration duration is variable, but the diff performs no polling and schedules no boundary calls while waiting.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change prevents premature single-model dispatch without adding work to the pending critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch a valid Git-backed or folderless quick-chat model comparison
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For an eligible draft, _send still calls SessionComparisonService.startComparison. The availability check now includes an in-memory repository-state read for workspace comparisons; quick chat returns before repository inspection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and send each configured comparison attempt through sessions management/provider boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two to ten attempts, matching the existing configured effective attempt count after variants; each attempt launches once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two-to-ten attempt launches occurred with the same Promise.all concurrency for eligible comparisons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All attempt launches are awaited with Promise.all before comparison startup completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider-backed model/session request for each comparison attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per effective attempt, two to ten; optional judge/synthesis work remains deferred and unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical request fan-out and concurrency existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Attempt request startup is on comparison launch's critical path; model completion continues asynchronously under existing lifecycle handling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective configured attempt count, bounded at 10 after model variants; folderless quick chat avoids repository checks entirely.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing Promise.all starts the bounded two-to-ten attempts concurrently. The PR does not change cardinality, grouping, limiter behavior, ordering, cancellation, or error cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model metadata lookup and committed selection behavior are unchanged. Cold/warm repository state only affects eligibility, not launch fan-out or request caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the send call path and startComparison implementation establish unchanged bounded fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and network duration vary, but the expensive fan-out is pre-existing and unchanged by the reviewed lines.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Eligible comparison launch cost and concurrency are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all six changed files and traced repository availability, retained-selection sends, pending configuration, and valid comparison launch paths. The diff adds only bounded observable reads/state derivations, avoids work for confirmed non-repositories, and does not increase existing comparison fan-out, retention, filesystem resolution, or UI-path synchronous work. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance finding was identified.
